title: Oracle computation and finite information

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: §15.1, printed/PDF p. 63: membership queries, the use principle and the closure formulation of Exercise 15.1; version 2024-02-25

summary: Add membership queries to finite programs, prove that a halting result uses finitely many oracle answers, and replace queries by computations.
abstract: A program can be given permission to ask whether a number belongs to a fixed set, even when no ordinary algorithm decides that set. Such an oracle answers each membership question, but the program must still perform its other calculations and may run forever. We extend an existing finite program language by this one operation and record the questions and answers in successful computations. Every halting result depends on only finitely many answers: changing the oracle elsewhere leaves that result intact. A finite beginning of a divergent computation gives no comparable guarantee. An explicit substitution of programs for queries then shows how one source of information can be simulated using another, and why a computable oracle adds no new partial functions.
